claims.claim: Martin's evocative storytelling style and gift for gripping narrative are mostly absent from the dry history.
claims.quote: mostly absent from this dry history

claims.claim: The Gyldayn attribution conjures unhappy Westerosi schoolchildren forced to study a weighty textbook.
Even the summary voice lands concrete, countable images, such as a dragon devouring a queen in six bites.
claims.quote: devoured the queen in six bites

claims.claim: Martin says Gyldayn is an opinionated man whose prejudices, gripes and cavils leak into the text, so the reader must remember they are reading the voice of a character.
claims.source: George R.R. Martin interviewed by Lenny Picker, Publishers Weekly, 16 Jul 2018
claims.quote: prejudices and gripes and his own cavils
claims.page: Imaginary History: PW Talks With George R.R. Martin

claims.claim: Martin dropped his own term 'fake history' for 'imaginary history' after readers took umbrage at the demeaning label.
claims.source: George R.R. Martin interviewed by Lenny Picker, Publishers Weekly, 16 Jul 2018
claims.quote: some of my readers actually took umbrage
claims.page: Imaginary History: PW Talks With George R.R. Martin

claims.claim: Martin calls the book essentially a popular history, not a novel, modelled on Costain's four-volume Plantagenet history and readable without prior knowledge.
claims.source: George R.R. Martin interviewed by Lenny Picker, Publishers Weekly, 16 Jul 2018
claims.page: Imaginary History: PW Talks With George R.R. Martin

claims.claim: Martin accepts the comparison to Tolkien's appendices and jokingly calls the book the GRRMarillion.
claims.source: George R.R. Martin interviewed by Lenny Picker, Publishers Weekly, 16 Jul 2018
claims.page: Imaginary History: PW Talks With George R.R. Martin

claims.claim: Martin insists the book is written in the style of a textbook, a quite different style adopted deliberately, and is not a traditional novel.
claims.source: George R.R. Martin interviewed by James Hibberd, Entertainment Weekly, 19 Nov 2018
claims.quote: written in the style of a textbook
claims.page: George R.R. Martin gets candid about new book

claims.claim: The history needs only one voice, Gyldayn's, whom Martin describes as a crotchety old academic, whereas the novels switch voice every chapter.
claims.source: George R.R. Martin interviewed by James Hibberd, Entertainment Weekly, 19 Nov 2018
claims.page: George R.R. Martin gets candid about new book

claims.claim: Martin found the book easy because it is linear: here is what happened in year 30, here is what happened in 25, with no juggling of parallel timelines.
claims.source: George R.R. Martin interviewed by James Hibberd, Entertainment Weekly, 19 Nov 2018
claims.quote: here's what happened in the year 30
claims.page: George R.R. Martin gets candid about new book

claims.claim: Martin invented contradictory imaginary primary sources, especially for the Dance of the Dragons, so he could tell the same events three different ways.
claims.source: George R.R. Martin interviewed by James Hibberd, Entertainment Weekly, 19 Nov 2018
claims.page: George R.R. Martin gets candid about new book

claims.claim: It is a generational story over 150 years in which a large cast are born, grow up, die and are succeeded by their children.
claims.source: George R.R. Martin interviewed by James Hibberd, Entertainment Weekly, 19 Nov 2018
claims.page: George R.R. Martin gets candid about new book

claims.claim: Martin likens Gyldayn to a modern historian of the Civil War who was not present and must reconstruct from memories and court records that sometimes contradict.
claims.source: George R.R. Martin interviewed by James Hibberd, Entertainment Weekly, 19 Nov 2018
claims.page: George R.R. Martin gets candid about new book

claims.claim: The text began as sidebars for The World of Ice and Fire that ballooned to 300,000 words and were pulled out to become the GRRM-arillion.
claims.source: George R.R. Martin interviewed by James Hibberd, Entertainment Weekly, 19 Nov 2018
claims.page: George R.R. Martin gets candid about new book

claims.claim: Martin stresses that the book is imaginary history, the essential point being the history part, and compares it to Costain's Plantagenets with dragons.
claims.source: George R.R. Martin, Not a Blog, 25 Apr 2018
claims.quote: The essential point being the 'history' part.
